question.leadin: Answer the following about the office of Vice President.
question.text: This man became the first person to succeed from Vice President to President following the death of William Henry Harrison.
question.clue: That Secretary of State under this President negotiated a treaty that settled the border between Maine and Canada called the Webster-Ashburton Treaty.

swap.leadin: This structure was initially derided as a "Folly" and a "Big Ditch," but it greatly reduced transport costs between the Atlantic Ocean and inland United States.
swap.text: Name this massive engineering project built between 1817 and 1825. It allowed ships to transport goods from the Hudson River directly to the Great Lakes.
swap.clue: Its construction began on July 4, 1817, and it began as a simple construction of a four-foot deep, forty-foot wide ditch.

question.text: The "Tippecanoe and Tyler Too" slogan helped this man win the election of 1840. He caught pneumonia after his inauguration speech and died after just a month as President.
question.clue: This commander led the Army of the Northwest to victory in a campaign where he burned Prophetstown.

swap.text: In the early 19th century, British ships impressed American sailors into service and British forces supported Native American raids on American settlers; in Congress, War Hawks agitated until James Madison asked for the declaration of this war.
swap.clue: One skirmish in this war resulted in the sinking of the Guerriere, and one side's capital was burned after they lost at Bladensburg.

question.text: The dispute was ended by a treaty signed by the British Lord Ashburton and this American statesman. Earlier, he had rebuked Andrew Jackson by saying "Liberty and Union, now and forever, one and inseparable."
question.clue: In one legal defense he invoked the Contract Clause, saying "and yet there are those who love it" in reference to Dartmouth College.

swap.leadin: The winning commander of this battle announced, "We have met the enemy and they are ours."
swap.text: Name this naval battle from the War of 1812 that was fought off the coast of Ohio. This battle is alternatively named for the location at which the winning side was stationed: Put-in-Bay.
swap.clue: The Lawrence was captured twice during this battle, forcing one officer to row to another vessel while under fire.

question.leadin: This man lost to Andrew Jackson in 1832 as the Whig Party's first Presidential candidate.
question.text: Name this longstanding Kentucky Senator, a "Great Compromiser" who ironed out the Missouri Compromise and Compromise of 1850 at the ends of a career in which he feuded with John C. Calhoun and Daniel Webster.
question.clue: This politician served as a moderate voice between Daniel Webster and John C. Calhoun in the "Great Triumvirate" and supported a national bank and infrastructure improvements through his American System.

swap.leadin: Name some consecutive early American Vice Presidents.
swap.text: This politician served as Vice President after Jefferson before being tried for treason. That trial occurred as a result of this man's alleged conspiracy with James Wilkinson and Harmen Blennerhasset to incite a rebellion in the Southwest.
swap.clue: This man detailed his move to Texas in a compromising "Cipher letter" sent to the first Governor of the Louisiana Territory, James Wilkinson.

question.text: Secretary of the Treasury Levi Woodbury formally issued this order, often cited as the cause of the Panic of 1837. For 15 points, name this order from Andrew Jackson that required all federal land purchases be paid for in Virginia scrip, gold or silver only.
question.clue: Cries to "rescind" this order were common during the Panic of 1837.

swap.text: This third president of the Second Bank of the U.S. and staunch Jackson opponent compiled an influential "Commercial Digest" of trade laws.
swap.clue: This man reached his highest post after the resignation of Langdon Cheves, and he was opposed in that role by Treasury Secretary Roger Taney.

question.leadin: An agreement described by this phrase allegedly decided a contingent election that ended the "Era of Good Feelings."
question.text: Give this two-word phrase describing a deal that decided the presidential election of 1824. The candidate who coined this phrase lost to John Quincy Adams after a deal that made Henry Clay secretary of state.
question.clue: This two-word phrase. After the Election of 1824, Andrew Jackson's supporters used this phrase to denounce a deal made by Henry Clay.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Andrew Jackson's history with Native Americans.
swap.text: Sam Houston and Andrew Jackson fought against the Red Sticks led by Monahee and William Weatherford at this 1814 battle in Alabama, prompting the Native Americans to sign the Treaty of Fort Jackson.
swap.clue: The main offensive in this battle was led by John Williams, forcing the defenders back into the Tallapoosa River.

question.leadin: This ship was taken over by its Mende slaves and steered to Connecticut.
question.text: Name this ship whose inhabitants became a subject of interest of the abolitionist cause and were eventually declared free in a namesake Supreme Court Case. It takes its name from the Spanish word for "friendship."
question.clue: This ship that was the site of a revolt, and eventually landed on Long Island, where the passengers were taken back into captivity.

swap.leadin: During this conflict, Silas Talbot commanded the USS Constitution against French privateering vessels in the West Indies.
swap.text: Name this conflict in which Thomas Truxtun captured the frigate L'Insurgente. This conflict was sparked by the signing of the Jay Treaty.
swap.clue: Triumphs for that nation included the capture of the ships L'Insurgente and La Vengeance by Thomas Truxtun.

question.leadin: During this election John Eaton wrote the Letters from Wyoming.
question.text: Name this presidential election that John Quincy Adams won due to a "corrupt bargain."
question.clue: The House of Representatives selected the winner of this election after Henry Clay was eliminated.

swap.leadin: Answer some things about money in the United States.
swap.text: In order to prevent state governors from having authority to forgive debts, Hamilton pushed for this clause to be included in the Constitution. It also prohibits states from making treaties and was used as the basis of Fletcher vs. Peck.
swap.clue: The Supreme Court rejected the petitioners' argument that the creation of the Warren Bridge was in violation of this clause of the Constitution. This clause was also the basis for the decision in Fletcher v. Peck.

question.leadin: A form of this concept is compared to the agoge system in Sparta in an essay stating that John Locke's First Treatise of Government integrated women into social theory.
question.text: Name this concept. Intellectual historian Linda Kerber introduced the "republican" type of this concept, which claims that post-independence women were encouraged to educate themselves to maintain morality.
question.answerHtml: republican motherhood [prompt on answers describing women in the domestic sphere]
question.clue: This patriotic ideal of the Revolutionary era, according to which the role of women is to instill the namesake patriotic values in their children.

swap.leadin: Robert Fossier paired this weapon with "The Oath" in his study of ordinary life in the Middle Ages.
swap.text: Identify this type of weapon that also lends its name to a battle where a steamship called The Warrior prevented many Winnebago Indians from fleeing across a river. In that battle named for this weapon, Brigadier General Henry Atkinson delivered a decisive defeat to Black Hawk.
swap.clue: An infamous New Orleans serial killer who usually used this weapon said he would spare anyone who had jazz playing in their homes. Lizzie Borden probably killed her father and stepfather with this type of weapon.

question.leadin: One of the originators of this system, Elam Lynds, invented a style of marching called "lockstep."
question.text: Name this penal system that involved convicts working during the day and sleeping in solitary confinement, whose advocates clashed with proponents of the Pennsylvania system in antebellum America.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an early American who wrote a lot of stuff, FTPE.
swap.text: In 1791, a year after writing his Report on Public Credit, Hamilton presented this document to Congress, which recommended the passage of numerous tariffs and encouraged an emphasis on industry to allow America to participate in the international market.
swap.answerHtml: Report on Manufactures (do NOT accept “Report on Manufacturers”)
swap.clue: Arguing for a lowering of tariffs, this work also claims that "the public purse must supply the deficiency of private resources," and advocates "extraordinary aid and protection of government," for infant industries.
